newsitem.title: CUBA: Senior Papal envoy to visit Cuba next month.
newsitem.headline: Senior Papal envoy to visit Cuba next month.

text.p: A senior Vatican official, Archbishop Jean-Louis Tauran, will travel to Cuba next month for a visit that could pave the way for a meeting between President Fidel Castro and Pope John Paul, diplomatic sources said on Tuesday.
The sources said Tauran, who is effectively the Vatican's foreign minister, would visit the communist-ruled island Oct. 25-29 at the invitation of the Cuban Foreign Ministry.
The sources said the trip might lead to a first meeting between the 76-year-old pontiff and Castro, 70, in Rome this November, although they cautioned it was still uncertain.
There had been speculation in recent weeks the two could meet if Castro attended the Nov. 13-17 summit in Rome organised by the U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Organisation.

Such a meeting would signal the extent to which relations between Cuban authorities and the Catholic Church have improved in recent months. The encounter would also raise the possibility of a subsequent papal trip to Cuba, the only Latin American nation the pontiff has not visited.
"The visit (by Tauran) takes place at a time of a general climate of a more positive relationship," said one source.

But Castro never announces his travel plans in advance and a Foreign Ministry spokesman, asked by reporters last week about a possible meeting with the pope, said it was too early to speculate. The spokesman noted relations with the church, however, were "nearer normality than abnormality."
Last week Castro talked to Papal Nuncio (Vatican ambassador) Beniamino Stella and to a senior Cuban cleric, Carlos Manuel de Cespedes, while attending a reception at the Chilean embassy.

Earlier this month Cuba's Cardinal Jaime Ortega, appointed by the pope in October 1994, indicated relations with the communist authorities were improving. In a homily, Ortega noted references to religion in an August document by the ruling Communist Party showed more acceptance of Christian beliefs.
Vatican representatives Cardinal Roger Etchegaray and Cardinal Carlo Furno visited Cuba in late 1994 and February 1996, respectively.

Cuban authorities began moving toward more relaxed relations with Christian churches in the early 1990s, after years of tension following the 1959 revolution that brought Castro to power. Membership in the Communist Party is no longer barred to the faithful, and constitutional changes in 1992 outlawed religious discrimination in clearer terms.
But ties with the Catholic Church have remained strained at times, notably over several calls in recent years by the island's Catholic bishops for political change.
The pope, while in frail health, has four trips abroad planned for next year. If he were to travel to Cuba, he could make the trip before or after a trip to Brazil expected in October.
